results.name: psf__requests-2148
results.summary: The bug is in requests/models.py: Response.iter_content()'s inner generate() only wraps IncompleteRead and DecodeError when consuming self.raw.stream(), so a raw socket.error (e.g. Errno 104 Connection reset by peer) raised by urllib3/httplib during a chunked read propagates unchanged through Response.content and Response.text. The fix is to import ConnectionError (and ProtocolError from urllib3.exceptions) in models.py and catch those around the raw.stream loop, re-raising them as requests.exceptions.ConnectionError (with the original error as reason) so callers get a unified requests exception while the traceback chain is preserved. A regression test simulating a socket.error during streaming content should be added to test_requests.py. No changes to adapters.py or exceptions.py are needed since ConnectionError already exists and is exported.

results.name: psf__requests-863
results.summary: Request.__init__ normalizes the hooks argument by iterating its items and calling register_hook(event=k, hook=v) once per (event, value) pair (requests/models.py lines 151-152). register_hook simply does self.hooks[event].append(hook) (line 466), so passing a list of callables as a value appends the list itself as one element, producing a nested list that fails when dispatch_hook iterates and tries to call a list. The consumption site requests/hooks.py dispatch_hook already handles both a bare callable (wrapping it in [hooks]) and an iterable of hooks, so the correct normalized shape is dict[event] -> list of callables. The minimal correct change is in Request.__init__: when the incoming value is a list/tuple, extend the per-event list with its elements (or register each element) instead of wrapping it; single callables should still become a one-element list, and the existing copy/defensive behavior (hooks = hooks or {}; iterating list(hooks.items())) should be preserved. Test coverage belongs in tests/test_requests.py alongside the existing hook tests (test_hook with hooks={'args': add_foo_header} at line 709 and test_multiple_hooks at line 713, which register hooks in a loop), adding a case where hooks={'response': [hook_a, hook_b]} dispatches both in order.

results.name: psf__requests-3362
results.summary: The behavior is intentional and comes from `stream_decode_response_unicode` (requests/utils.py): when `decode_unicode=True` it only decodes if `r.encoding` is truthy, otherwise it yields the raw byte chunks unchanged. For `application/json` responses, `r.encoding` is `None` (no charset in Content-Type, and requests only sets encoding from the Content-Type header), so `iter_content(..., decode_unicode=True)` yields bytes. `Response.text`, by contrast, explicitly falls back to `self.apparent_encoding` (chardet) when `self.encoding is None`, so it returns unicode. The `iter_content` docstring claim that content is decoded 'using the best available encoding based on the response' is misleading because it implies `decode_unicode=True` always returns unicode, like `.text`. Recommended minimal change: clarify the `iter_content` docstring (and optionally the streaming docs) that `decode_unicode=True` only decodes when `Response.encoding` is set (it does not use `apparent_encoding`), and note the existing test that encodes this assumption.

results.name: psf__requests-1963
results.summary: The bug is in SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects in requests/sessions.py. Each iteration unconditionally starts from the original request via `prepared_request = req.copy()` (line 91) and derives `method = req.method` (line 102), so method rewrites performed on earlier hops (e.g., 303 converting POST to GET) are discarded and later 307/308 redirects re-send the original method. The minimal fix is to chain from the previously issued prepared request (the prior hop's prepared_request) instead of the original `req`, and derive the redirect method from that prior request so the 303/301/302 rewrite rules apply to the current method rather than the original. PreparedRequest.copy (requests/models.py) already duplicates method, headers, body, and cookies, so it is the correct carrier for this state; it needs no change but is the supporting location. Scope should remain limited to resolve_redirects.

results.name: django__django-11001
results.summary: The bug is that SQLCompiler.ordering_parts regex r'(.*)\s(ASC|DESC)(.*)' with re's default non-multiline behavior only sees the last physical line of a multiline RawSQL ordering expression when using search(). In get_order_by(), `without_ordering = self.ordering_parts.search(sql).group(1)` therefore produces just the trailing line fragment (e.g. 'then 2 else 1 end' / 'else null end'), causing distinct multiline RawSQL clauses with identical last lines to be wrongly deduplicated against the `seen` set. The same pattern is duplicated in get_extra_select() for distinct queries. Fix: normalize sql to a single line (e.g. `sql_oneline = ' '.join(sql.split('\n'))`, or split() to also collapse \r) before calling ordering_parts.search in both locations, leaving the seen/add logic and regex unchanged. Add a regression test in tests/ordering/tests.py (near test_order_by_f_expression_duplicates) using two multiline RawSQL order_by expressions whose last lines match, asserting both survive in the compiled SQL.

results.name: sympy__sympy-12454
results.summary: The bug is in Matrix.is_upper in sympy/matrices/matrices.py (lines 1113-1115): it iterates 'j in range(i)' without limiting to self.cols, so a 4x2 (tall) matrix indexes column 2 out of range. Fix by bounding the inner loop, e.g. 'j in range(min(i, self.cols))'. is_lower is not affected because it delegates to _eval_is_lower (lines 622-625), which already uses 'range(i + 1, self.cols)' and is safe for wide matrices; only verification/regression tests are warranted there. Add regression cases for tall/wide rectangular zero matrices next to the existing test_is_upper/test_is_lower tests.

results.name: sympy__sympy-20154
results.summary: partitions() reuses and mutates a single dict instance across iterations, yielding ms (and (sum, ms) for size=True) at two sites. Fix: yield copies (e.g. yield sum(ms.values()), ms.copy() / yield ms.copy()) so each result is independent, and update the docstring to remove the 'same dictionary object is returned' caveat and the p.copy() workaround examples. Tests that defensively copy (test_partitions, test_uniq) remain valid but can be simplified; no non-test caller depends on identity reuse.
